canonical_topic: Crude oil trading units: barrel and tonne
definition: Crude oil is traded by volume (barrels) in the U.S. and by weight (tonnes) in Europe, with an approximate conversion between the two that varies by crude type.
core_idea: Because different crude oils have different densities, there is no single exact barrel-to-tonne conversion factor — it must be looked up per crude type, ranging roughly from 7.2 (Persian Gulf) to 7.5 (premium light crude like WTI/Brent) barrels per tonne.
key_points: Rough rule of thumb: ~7.5 barrels per tonne of crude oil.
Actual ratio depends on crude composition/density: ~7.2 bbl/tonne for Persian Gulf crude up to ~7.5 bbl/tonne for premium light crude (WTI, Brent).
trading_implications: Converting volumes between U.S. (barrel-quoted) and European (tonne-quoted) markets requires using the correct crude-specific ratio, not a single universal constant.
caveats: Assuming one fixed barrels-per-tonne number applies to all crude oils — the author states the ratio varies with crude composition.
